description: The numeric guard `grep -qE '^[0-9.]+$'` for CAP_REV (loop.sh:42) accepts any run of digits and dots including malformed multi-dot values ('1.2.3', '.', '..', '1..2') since the pattern places no constraint on how many dots appear or their position, before handing the value to `awk "BEGIN{exit !($CAP_REV>0)}"`. Under the current python `round(x,2)` producer this specific malformation cannot occur today, so it is latent rather than firing, but it is a known-and-already-documented class of defect: the sibling founder-loop.sh was reviewed and flagged for the IDENTICAL weak-numeric-guard pattern (its own adversarial history, FIND-903, calls out 'TOTAL should be validated as a single well-formed number'). This exact lesson was not carried over into lm-capafy-loop.sh, which duplicates the same loose-guard shape for a different revenue field.

evidence.snippet: if printf '%s' "$CAP_REV" | grep -qE '^[0-9.]+$' && awk "BEGIN{exit !($CAP_REV>0)}" 2>/dev/null; then STATUS="EARNING (Capafy net \$$CAP_REV) — grow it"; fi

fix: Use a strict single-decimal numeric pattern, e.g. `^-?[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?$`, matching the hardening already recommended for founder-loop.sh's TOTAL guard.
